narratives.Overview:
1. Recut P1 claim-first on cold, rearm, and ready: at dispatch SHA `805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc`, move `persistOccupancyOrDeny` to immediately after identity resolve on `session:start` cold/rearm (replace previews at session-start.ts 1578 and 2135) and replace `session:ready` preview at 243. Reuse the requirements posture order at 1473. Dest-mutating work waits on persist. Ritual-state and session-bind stay after persist.
2. Recut P1 closed occupancy-gated writes: linked-worktree deposit reconstitution including VERSION repair (`applyLinkedWorktreeDeposit` / `reconstituteLinkedWorktreeDeposit`); `session:ready` parent-path cache fetch-all/refresh-closed before `finishReady`. Observability JSONL (triage/value/eval history, process-cost `.deft-cache/events.jsonl`) is a separate class. Shared finalize-owed refs are a separate class. Ritual-state is not this hole.
3. Recut P1 #4444 rollback: release only a persist-time `claimed` or `stolen` lease this invocation wrote, and only when this invocation never aligned occupancy with ritual. Do not release `heartbeat`. Do not key rollback on preview `action: "claimed"`. Keep `ritualPersistenceTransitionError` keep-lease recovery for post-persist ritual failure. Do not reuse `releaseOccupancy` as unconditional rollback; condition compare-and-delete of the acquired record under `withOccupancyLock`. Carry acquisition across nested start. Steal claim-first must name restore-previous versus release-to-empty before steal moves earlier than orientation.
4. Recut P1 ready two claim sites: claim before reconstitution and before parent-path cache fetch-all; nested `session:start` persist is the invocation lease; `finishReady` heartbeats when nested start already persisted. Do not double-steal.
5. Recut P1 barrier tests: winner/loser uses distinct resolved owners. Same-id heartbeat stays a characterization test. Do not promise two OS processes with one session id serialize via moving `write=true`. Occupancy-stress worker pattern points at `session:start` dest files, not occupancy.json alone. Failure-path assertions cover pre-preview process-cost writes or an explicit narrowed guarantee for that class.
6. Recut P1 tests: `[false, true]` occupancy write-order pins in session-start-rearm.test.ts 353/404, session-ready.test.ts 254/387, and session-start.test.ts 1117 change to claim-first.
7. Preserve: `withOccupancyLock` live re-read; identity mint-refusal; primary/sibling fences; process-only and read-only claim-free paths; #4625 advisory occupancy for lifecycle complete/check.
8. Exclude: holding `withOccupancyLock` across doctor/orientation (#3736); instruction-only occupancy as AC discharge; a new lock family; treating occupancy as a success-gated last write that reorders ritual.

issueCommentThread.body:
### v0.108.0 release audit

**Result: partially addressed; the reported startup race remains.**

The release includes two adjacent hardenings. [PR #3763](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3763) binds one session identity across occupancy preview, nested startup work, and the final claim. [PR #3870](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3870) changes mutation-hook ordering so a session rejected by the write gate cannot first rewrite the occupant's ritual record. These changes improve identity propagation and the host write-gate path, but they do not move session-start occupancy acquisition ahead of startup mutations.

In the tagged source, `session:start` still performs a non-writing preview first ([source](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts#L1342-L1345)), can run orientation and history-producing work before ownership ([source](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts#L1511-L1601), [source](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts#L1624-L1679)), and persists occupancy only near successful completion ([source](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts#L1740-L1751)). `session:ready` likewise previews occupancy and defers the write claim to `finishReady()` ([source](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-ready.ts#L196-L227)); verification and cache recovery can occur before that claim.

Released tests expect preview-then-write ordering (`[false, true]`) rather than acquire-first behavior ([session:start test](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start-rearm.test.ts#L209-L260), [session:ready test](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-ready.test.ts#L190-L246)). The release therefore does not yet prove that ownership precedes the first startup mutation, that a losing process performs no startup writes, or that an acquire-first failure releases its lease.

charter: refutation

The core ordering claim survives refutation. Acquire-before-startup-mutation is compatible with advisory occupancy; #4625 does not justify leaving these two cooperating startup commands racing. Three requirements need sharper boundaries before implementation.

Verification: read the issue body and comments through the inclusive ceiling; inspected the pinned source and ran static assertions for preview → deposit → persist ordering, the existing `[false, true]` test assertions, and the release input shape. No runtime two-process test was run. The tests cited below were inspected, not executed. The panel deposit matches the envelope ceiling; panel completeness is not observable from this seat.

Existing mechanisms: `applyWorktreeOccupancy` already takes `withOccupancyLock`, re-reads occupancy under it, rejects a foreign live owner, and publishes a fenced record (occupancy.ts:1388–1477). It distinguishes `claimed` from `heartbeat`. `releaseOccupancy` also locks, but authorizes by current session identity or expiry (1755–1847). `session:ready` resolves one identity, propagates it into nested start, avoids repeating steal after nested acquisition, and checks ritual ownership after the final claim (session-ready.ts:203–221, 278–327, 434–474). Reuse these mechanisms; this is not a missing-lock or identity-propagation redesign.

## C1. Rollback needs acquisition provenance, not just an owner id — sharpens-framing

Evidence: the locked claim preserves `claimedAt` for a live same-owner heartbeat and returns `heartbeat` versus `claimed` (occupancy.ts:1429, 1460). The release API accepts session id, environment, time, closeout and lock dependencies, but no expected acquisition identity; its ownership check compares session ids, and expired records can also be released (1755–1786). Ready's nested-start flag tracks an occupancy result with the matching session id, not whether this invocation newly acquired the lease (session-ready.ts:462–474).

Failure mode: a naive finally/release by session id deletes a pre-existing lease after a failed rearm. Even remembering “I acquired” is insufficient if that lease was released and replaced under the same id before cleanup. Nested start can also succeed while outer ready subsequently fails verification; inner success must not silently settle outer cleanup ownership.

Disposition: retain the existing “release only the invocation's acquired lease” criterion, but make it testable: distinguish borrowed/heartbeat occupancy from acquisition, carry the acquisition across nested start, and condition rollback under the existing lock on the acquisition still being current. Test pre-existing same-owner, replacement, nested-start success followed by ready failure, and thrown errors. Do not substitute the general release verb as unconditional rollback; it also runs consumer-header enforcement (1796–1809).

## C2. The mutation inventory starts before occupancy preview — sharpens-framing

Evidence: rearm-ineligible and cold Git-error returns call `emitSessionStartProcessCost` before their respective previews (session-start.ts:1549–1559 vs 1578; 2116–2125 vs 2135). That emitter delegates to lifecycle events and documents its default append to `.deft-cache/events.jsonl` (process-cost.ts:1–5, 147–197). Independently, the advertised race remains: deposit reconstitution occurs after preview and before persist in both startup paths (1585/1755, 2142/2619) and ready (243/260/284). Reconstitution performs mkdir/copy into the destination (init-deposit/gitignore.ts:933–943, 1065–1067).

Failure mode: merely moving the final claim to the current preview site fixes the normal-path deposit race but leaves early-failure local writes unowned. A happy-path two-process test will miss this. Calling an append “telemetry” does not make it read-only; calling deposit copies idempotent does not make them non-mutating.

Disposition: keep the whole-command inventory criterion and explicitly include pre-preview failures and diagnostic/event writes. Buffer, suppress, or place those outside the shared session-state boundary with an explicit narrowed guarantee. Require failure-path assertions as well as the normal collision barrier. This sharpens the existing acceptance criterion rather than adding a new startup subsystem.

## C3. Define the race as distinct resolved owners, or explicitly add same-owner serialization — sharpens-framing

Evidence: `applyWorktreeOccupancy` rejects only a different live session id and admits the same id as heartbeat (occupancy.ts:1412–1460). The pinned module explicitly documents payload hosts whose parent and children share an id, and a cooperative bearer-id boundary rather than authentication (15–28, 46–65).

Failure mode: two OS processes presenting the same resolved owner both pass even after acquire-first. Therefore an unqualified promise that “two processes race, exactly one proceeds” exceeds the existing occupancy abstraction. An injected owner string or inherited shared identity is not proof that the caller acquired this invocation's lease.

Disposition: specify distinct resolved owners for the required winner/loser barrier test, and add a same-owner characterization test. If same-owner startup serialization is required, name that separate critical section explicitly; moving `write=true` cannot provide it. Keep identity mint-refusal, primary/sibling fences, member-versus-owner restrictions and process-only/read-only exceptions intact. This is the injection/swarm boundary, not an authorization guarantee against hostile same-user code.

## C4. “Final-success write” is useful shorthand, not literally the last possible failure — footnote

Ready re-inspects ritual after claiming and can return failure with occupancy held (session-ready.ts:297–327). Start also writes its ritual after persist. The accurate target is late acquisition after earlier mutations, rather than a claim guaranteed to occur only on successful commands.

Road not taken: treating occupancy's advisory status as permission to keep startup writes before acquisition. Its strongest case is that lifecycle complete/check and unknown-lease product writes intentionally remain independent of occupancy; #4625's accepted map 5703321854 preserves that distinction. But this issue concerns commands already participating in occupancy coordination. The pinned mkdir/copy paths defeat the “all pre-claim work is read-only” alternative. I would change that verdict if the inventory demonstrated that every such effect had been removed or isolated, with the narrower guarantee stated explicitly. Retain acquire-first for startup and leave the broader lifecycle policy unchanged.

## Round 1 critic (refutation) — #3906

Charter: refutation. Target: "occupancy is a final-success write rather than a prerequisite for startup mutations." All reads pinned to `805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc`. Input ceiling 6181795668 (inclusive). No sibling posts read.

### Verdict

**The target survives.** On both mutation paths, the first `write=true` occupancy call comes after state-writing work. But the issue lists the wrong writes and has two acceptance criteria that cannot bind as written. One of them contradicts an existing held-lease contract.

No embedded instructions found in the issue body or in-envelope comments.

### Inventory (verified by reading the code, not the cited line numbers)

- `session-start.ts` rearm path: preview at 1578 (`write=false`), then `applyLinkedWorktreeDeposit` at 1585, then `persistOccupancyOrDeny` at 1755. Cold path: preview at 2135, deposit at 2142, persist at 2619.
- Existing acquire-first pattern in the same file: the requirements posture calls `persistOccupancyOrDeny` (1473) **before** `runReadOnlySessionStart` and `persistSessionPosture`.
- `withOccupancyLock` (`occupancy.ts:2958`) already serializes the persist and re-checks the live occupant under the lock. Two racing claims already fail closed at the claim. What is missing is the **order**, not a lock.
- `releaseOccupancy` (`occupancy.ts:1755`) is the only release primitive.

### Findings

**1. `blocks-the-design` — "release on failure" contradicts the existing held-on-failure contract, and there is no primitive that can release "only what this invocation acquired".**
- Evidence: `ritualPersistenceTransitionError` (`session-start.ts:499-506`) keeps the lease held when the ritual-state write fails after the claim. It tells the operator to re-run with the same `--session-id`. `session:ready` does the same on a post-claim ritual-owner mismatch (`session-ready.ts:311-314`: "occupancy is held by …"; no release). `releaseOccupancy` checks ownership only by session id (`owns`, `occupancy.ts:1785`). It also runs the session-exit gate `enforceConsumerHeaderPlaceholderWhenProductEvidence` (1800), which can deny the release.
- Failure mode: a rearm caller already holds a live lease under the same id. Preview and persist both return `heartbeat`. Under claim-first, a later finalize-owed block (1640 area) causes a rollback through `releaseOccupancy`. That drops the caller's **pre-existing** lease mid-session, and the hooks then deny that session's own writes. The opposite case also fails: on a tree with product evidence, the exit gate denies the release, so a failed start leaves a lease stuck.
- Disposition consequence: AC3 cannot bind as written. The lean must (a) choose between the existing hold-and-re-run contract and release-on-failure, at least for the post-claim ritual-write failure, and (b) say that rollback applies only when the write-claim action is `claimed` (a fresh acquire). `heartbeat` keeps the lease. `stolen` needs its own stated outcome. Rollback must compare-and-delete the exact acquired record under `withOccupancyLock`. It must not reuse `releaseOccupancy`.

**2. `sharpens-framing` — the Expected list names the wrong state: ritual-state and session-bind are already fenced.**
- Evidence: in `session:start`, `writeRitualState` (1792 rearm, 2673 cold) and `bindSessionGeneration` (1829, 2778) all run **after** `persistOccupancyOrDeny`. The verified pre-claim writes are:
  - `session:start`: linked deposit reconstitution (1585/2142), triage-welcome history (`writeHistory` default true at 2473), value and eval readback history (2555, 2566), the staleness tickler (2532), and the finalize-owed private fetch. That fetch force-writes `refs/deft/finalize-owed/<branch>` (`finalize-owed.ts:575+`).
  - `session:ready`: deposit reconstitution (260), and cache recovery (504+) on the path where the quick ritual is already bound to this id but the lease is free. In that case the nested start does not run, so nothing has claimed yet.
  - `session:ready` runs its nested start with `writeHistory: false`, so triage history is not a `session:ready` pre-claim write.
- Failure mode: an implementer writes the AC5 barrier test against ritual or session-bind writes. It passes today, so it proves nothing, and the real pre-claim writes stay unfenced.
- Disposition consequence: replace the Expected list with this verified list, and point AC5 at triage, readback, and cache writes.

**3. `sharpens-framing` — "the losing process performs no session writes" cannot be met while failed-attempt telemetry and shared refs exist.**
- Evidence: `emitSessionStartProcessCost` intentionally records failed attempts, including deny paths (`#2994`, comments at 1549, 1794, 2115, 2675). The finalize-owed ref is in the shared git common dir. Sibling worktrees that hold their **own** leases fetch the same ref, so a per-worktree claim cannot fence it.
- Failure mode: AC5 either fails forever, or is "fixed" by deleting the #2994 failed-attempt records, which is a gate-integrity regression.
- Disposition consequence: AC1 needs three classes, not two: worktree session state (fence behind the claim), attempt telemetry (exempt, append-only), and shared idempotent caches or refs (exempt, or fenced separately). AC5 then says "no worktree-session-state writes".

**4. `sharpens-framing` — contenders with the same identity are out of reach.**
- Evidence: preview and persist deny only when `live.sessionId !== incoming` (`occupancy.ts:1360`, and the matching check under the lock). The same id gets `heartbeat`. On `payload` hosts the parent and its subagents share one id (`occupancy.ts:47-52`).
- Failure mode: two processes with one id both pass claim-first and both write. A barrier test built that way fails no matter what the remedy is.
- Disposition consequence: scope AC5 to **distinct resolved owners**. Either declare the same-id race out of scope, or add a per-invocation nonce. The nonce is a larger change and should be a separate issue.

**5. `sharpens-framing` — reuse the existing claim-first ordering; do not invent a new mechanism.**
- Evidence: the requirements posture at 1473 already persists before doing any work, and the lock already makes the claim fail closed (see Inventory).
- Failure mode: a new lease or lock layer duplicates `withOccupancyLock` and splits the source of truth.
- Disposition consequence: the remedy is to move `persistOccupancyOrDeny` up to replace the previews at 1578 and 2135, and to replace `session-ready.ts:243`, plus the rollback from finding 1. The `[false, true]` assertions in `session-start-rearm.test.ts:351-353, 403-404` and `session-ready.test.ts:254, 387` are expected to change to claim-first.

**6. `footnote`** — The `write=false` preview returns `action: "claimed"` and the message "occupancy claimed session …" when nothing was written (`occupancy.ts:1374-1385`). This misleads log readers. It goes away on the mutation path if claim-first lands.

**7. `footnote`** — Swarm/injection lens: today the losing process can copy `.deft/core` into a linked worktree it never owns. The bytes come from the same payload source, so integrity risk is low. A concurrent `copyFileSync` onto the same files can briefly expose a truncated file to the winner's reads. Real-world exposure is mostly operator or host double-starts, because the implement-class dest-lock (#4066) already prevents double dispatch into one dest.

### Road not taken

I rejected "reclassify the pre-claim writes as non-mutations". Steelman: it is the smallest diff and keeps #2994 telemetry. It fails because triage history and readback history are durable session records that a later worker reads as its own. What would change my verdict: proof that every pre-claim write is idempotent and keyed per invocation.

I also rejected "align with instruction-only occupancy (#4625)", because the hook write gate enforces this fence in code.

Refutation target (Stop 1 comment 6181716723): occupancy is a final-success write rather than a prerequisite for startup mutations.

## Verdict

At dispatch SHA `805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc` the target's second clause holds for cold/rearm `session:start` and for `session:ready`: dest-mutating work runs after a non-locking `write=false` preview and before `persistOccupancyOrDeny` / `claimOnSuccess`. The first clause overstates that machinery. Occupancy persist on those paths is a late exclusive step; `writeRitualState` follows it; occupancy stays held when `ready=false` after tools failure; requirements posture already persists occupancy before its first posture write. Persist itself already admits only one live lease under `withOccupancyLock`. The live hole is loser dest writes in the preview-persist window, including a single process that reconstitutes then exits on finalize-owed.

A successor lean that binds the target as written will treat occupancy as a success-gated last write and will churn ritual order that already waits.

## 1. Expected-behavior bag treats already-waiting ritual as the same hole as dest identity copies (blocks-the-design)

Evidence. Pin-read `git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts` (blob `c6d0dd2624012745d270330e05e68fce96e01443`). `runOccupancy` 1275-1284 takes `write`. Rearm: preview 1578 (`false`), `applyLinkedWorktreeDeposit` 1585, finalize-owed abort 1632-1652, `persistOccupancyOrDeny` 1755 (`true` via 1369), `writeRitualState` 1792. Cold: preview 2135, deposit 2142, triage welcome `writeHistory` default true 2473, value/eval readback history 2555/2566, finalize-owed abort 2589-2610, persist 2619, `writeRitualState` 2673. Pin-read `git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/init-deposit/gitignore.ts` (blob `a9d50be49948c1bd504393cd9f12d106e63e5c11`): `reconstituteLinkedWorktreeDeposit` `mkdirSync`/`copyFileSync` of `.deft/core` and may write `VERSION`; it never copies occupancy/ritual files. Pin-read `git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/session/session-ready.ts` (blob `04af9aa135a4c2e2baf278af39364ea48d0f7a18`): preview 243-256, reconstitution 257-277, `claimOnSuccess`/`finishReady` 278-283, cache `fetchAll`/`refreshClosed` into `.deft-cache` 521-535 still before that claim on the parent path. Pin-read `git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts` (blob `0d3d7f54a2c5a1efab4b13600c0e98e69a8f36a8`): `write=false` returns `action: "claimed"` with no `withOccupancyLock` (1374-1390); persist locks and re-reads (1391+). Issue expected behavior groups orientation, cache recovery, history, ritual, and session-bind as one acquire-before list. Ritual and session-bind already wait on persist.

Failure mode. Two mutation `session:start` processes both pass preview on an unoccupied tree. Both can copy dest `.deft/core` (and append history JSONL). Persist then admits one lease. The loser already wrote dest identity. A later worker treats that payload as owned local state. A two-process test that watches only `occupancy.json` and ritual-state stays green. A lean that implements the expected-behavior list as a unit will move persist relative to `writeRitualState` (already ordered) and can leave `applyLinkedWorktreeDeposit` pre-claim because that helper's comment excludes occupancy/ritual.

Disposition consequence. The lean cannot bind that list as one hole. Closed occupancy-gated writes: linked-worktree deposit reconstitution including VERSION repair; `session:ready` cache fetch-all/refresh-closed on the parent path before `finishReady`. Observability JSONL (triage/value/eval history, process-cost `.deft-cache/events.jsonl`) is a separate class. Ritual-state stays post-persist.

## 2. Recut P1 to the preview-persist window (sharpens-framing)

Evidence. Persist uses `withOccupancyLock` and re-reads live occupancy. `git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/session/occupancy-stress.test.ts` already proves persist workers do not interleave live leases (workers call `applyWorktreeOccupancy` then `releaseOccupancy`; they never run `session:start`). Requirements path `runRequirementsSessionStart` persists occupancy at 1473 before posture write. Read-only posture never calls occupancy (`git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/session/session-start.test.ts` around 1117-1134). Finalize-owed can return after reconstitution and before persist, so one process writes dest payload and exits with no lease.

Failure mode. Binding "final-success write" hides that dual-lease is already fail-closed and that the remaining hole is dest writes in the unlocked window. Binding "every occupancy consumer claim-first" recuts product-worker occupancy, which this issue leaves closed.

Disposition consequence. Recut P1 to: cold/rearm/ready run dest-mutating startup work in a preview-persist window; persist is the first locked occupancy write; ritual-state already waits. Default remedy: reuse requirements claim-first (`persistOccupancyOrDeny` immediately after identity resolve, then dest mutations, then ritual) on those three paths.

## 3. Release-on-failure must reuse #4444 claimed/stolen vs heartbeat (sharpens-framing)

Evidence. `git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts` 1494-1506: requirements rollback calls `releaseOccupancy` only when `persisted.action` is `claimed` or `stolen`. `git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/session/session-start-read-only.test.ts` pins that rollback and pins that a heartbeat is not released. Cold/rearm ritual-write failure throws `ritualPersistenceTransitionError` (499-507, 1807, 2688): occupancy is held; recovery is same-id rearm/cold. Steal preview at occupancy.ts 1624-1636 reports `action: "stolen"` with no write; persist then replaces the prior occupant. `write=false` already reports `action: "claimed"` with no file.

Failure mode. Claim-first plus "release when startup fails before a usable mutation session" applied to cold/rearm will release after orientation/tools failure and drop same-id recovery, or steal-then-fail then `occupancy:release` and empty the tree. A rollback keyed on preview `action: "claimed"` will call release against a lease this invocation never wrote.

Disposition consequence. Bind the #4444 rule: release only a persist-time `claimed` or `stolen` lease this invocation wrote, and only when this invocation never aligned occupancy with ritual (requirements-style). Keep `ritualPersistenceTransitionError` keep-lease recovery for post-persist ritual failure. Steal claim-first must name restore-previous versus release-to-empty before steal moves earlier than orientation.

## 4. session:ready has two claim sites (sharpens-framing)

Evidence. Ready previews at 243, reconstitutes at 257, nested `session:start` at 437-478 can persist occupancy (`nestedStartClaimedOccupancy = true`; nested `writeHistory` defaults false at 442), cache recovery at 502-535 can still run, then `finishReady` claims again.

Failure mode. Treating ready as one preview-then-claim pair will double-steal, or miss that cache recovery after nested start already runs under a live nested lease while the parent-only path still fetch-alls before any persist.

Disposition consequence. Ready AC: claim before reconstitution and before parent-path cache fetch-all; nested start persist is the invocation lease; `finishReady` heartbeats when nested start already persisted.

## 5. Tests pin preview-then-write as the current contract (footnote)

`git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/session/session-start-rearm.test.ts` (blob `b16f1503c4c20c739cb0417026ac16d78b2c223a`) 353 and 404; `git show 805209c849cac0481f780108c8e78a4c5b7cb3bc:packages/core/src/session/session-ready.test.ts` (blob `7ae30b1a86b841d72fcd8259562d4c4712c8eae6`) 254 and 387; also `session-start.test.ts` 1117 (absent from the issue body) expect occupancy `write` order `[false, true]`. Occupancy-stress covers persist exclusion, not session:start dest writes. Issue body line cites are v0.108.0; the dispatch-SHA lines above supersede them.

## Injection / swarm

The target changes shared worktree identity. `reconstituteLinkedWorktreeDeposit` copies `.deft/core` into dest. Later workers treat that payload as owned local state. Unique dest-lock is implement-class. Two mutation `session:start` on one unoccupied tree is the cooperative collision occupancy serializes. Leaving reconstitution in the unlocked preview window lets both processes write dest identity and then contend on the lease.

## Inventory (reuse)

- `persistOccupancyOrDeny` + `withOccupancyLock` + live re-read
- `evaluateOccupancyCeremonyEligibility` (side-effect-free eligibility)
- requirements claim-first + claimed/stolen rollback (#4444)
- `releaseOccupancy`
- occupancy-stress worker spawn pattern, pointed at `session:start` dest files
- read-only posture already claim-free and ritual-free
- #3769 / PR #3870 occupancy-before-ritual-persist on the hook dispatcher (different path)
- occupancy.ts header: advisory same-machine coordination; do not claim #4625 as AC discharge for this module

## Road taken

Move `persistOccupancyOrDeny` to immediately after identity resolve on cold/rearm/ready (requirements shape), then dest mutations, then ritual-state, with #4444 rollback. Preview may remain `write=false` or `evaluateOccupancyCeremonyEligibility` for deny-early; dest copies wait on persist.

Road closed: hold `withOccupancyLock` across doctor/orientation. occupancy.ts residual records that denying owners while the sidecar lock is held is the #3736 load-shedding regression; the live lease record is the fence.

Road closed: instruction-only occupancy (#4625) leaving the preview window. Persist already serializes leases; dest identity copies are this issue.

Steelman for classify-writes: dests whose reconstitution status is `already-present` or `skipped` (framework source) copy nothing, and leftover writes are history JSONL. Flip condition: a linked dest missing `.deft/core` copies payload before persist. That path is the swarm identity case. Classify-writes still has to move reconstitution after persist, which is claim-first under another name.

## Status

Confirmed against v0.108.0 and current `master`. Identity propagation was hardened, but startup still performs mutations before it owns the worktree occupancy lease.

## Summary

Acquire and fence worktree occupancy before the first mutation performed by `session:start` or `session:ready`.

## Confirmed implementation evidence

- `session:start` performs a non-writing occupancy preview first: [`session-start.ts:1342-1345`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts#L1342-L1345).
- It can persist orientation state and write triage/session history before ownership: [`session-start.ts:1511-1601`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts#L1511-L1601), [`session-start.ts:1624-1679`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts#L1624-L1679).
- The lease is persisted only near successful completion: [`session-start.ts:1740-1751`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts#L1740-L1751).
- `session:ready` likewise previews first and claims in `finishReady()`: [`session-ready.ts:196-227`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-ready.ts#L196-L227).
- Released tests assert preview-then-write ordering (`[false, true]`): [`session-start-rearm.test.ts:209-260`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-start-rearm.test.ts#L209-L260), [`session-ready.test.ts:190-246`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/session-ready.test.ts#L190-L246).

## Reproduction

1. Start two mutation sessions concurrently in the same unoccupied worktree.
2. Barrier both processes after the occupancy preview.
3. Allow both to execute pre-claim startup steps.
4. Allow both to attempt the final claim.
5. Observe that the losing process can perform startup writes before it is denied.

## Expected behavior

Read-only inspection may precede the claim. Before orientation, cache recovery, history, ritual, session-bind, or other session state can be written, the command must atomically acquire occupancy for the invocation's resolved owner.

If startup later fails before yielding a usable mutation session, it must release only the lease it acquired. Successful startup preserves that lease. Explicit read-only startup must remain claim-free and mutation-free.

## Actual gap

Occupancy is currently a final-success write rather than a prerequisite for startup mutations. Two conforming sessions can both pass preview and mutate shared state before one final claim succeeds.

## Already delivered

- [x] Pass one resolved owner identity through preview, nested startup, and final claim — delivered by [PR #3763](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3763).
- [x] Deny a host-hook write before rewriting a foreign occupant's ritual record — delivered by [PR #3870](https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3870).

These harden adjacent paths but do not establish acquire-before-mutate ordering.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Classify every pre-claim startup step as read-only or mutating.
- [ ] Acquire occupancy atomically before the first mutating step.
- [ ] Release only the invocation's acquired lease when startup fails before producing a usable mutation session.
- [ ] Preserve the lease when startup succeeds.
- [ ] Add a deterministic two-process barrier test proving that the losing process performs no session writes.
- [ ] Cover both `session:start` and `session:ready`, including cache-recovery and nested-start paths.
- [ ] Verify that read-only session start never claims occupancy or writes session state.
